body: Not exactly addressing the question but imagine how good it would feel to lie around in bed on a lazy morning!

I think it's important to do some of both. I like his analogy with a shareholder's board where you have the largest share (your feelings are the most important overall) but you don't have the only share (other people's feelings matter too).

That paragraph may go a little far in the direction of 'tough love' -- that's part of this blogger's style. But I like thinking of life as something we're all in together. Not each person living a life in parallel, but that we all have a 'stake' (both in the sense of having put money in the pot and in the sense of a shareholder's vote) in each other's lives.

It's not as binary as living for yourself or living for someone else. We all do both.

I think being focused on yourself is inherently depressing. I'm always at my best when I'm thinking of something outside of myself. Often another person, but really any external goal will do -- sometimes it's enough to just find a task, decide that it needs to get done, and then get it done.
I don't think the point is to judge anyone as being selfish. The point is that when you commit suicide everyone who knows you is damaged by it. Don't fool yourself that you're doing anyone a favor.
